rationale: bugs_open/385 §5c (cause established 2026-08-25, first-hand at every joint): on 2026-08-23 a build-arm rebuild of loancalculator.co.uk/tools/loan-vs-savings.html appended a byte-identical, component_id-NULL copy of the page's locked calculator beside the locked row, and the page then failed every re-render (self-perpetuating). The writer is save_page_sections_action.go's Layer 2 interactive-preservation block: its preload (build_status='deployed' AND interactive) selected the locked row — measured 2026-08-25, the ONLY locked row in the fleet satisfying that predicate, which is why nine sibling pages in the same wave were untouched — and its matcher judged 'is this stored tool already in the incoming set?' by EXACT SLOT-NAME STRING only. On the build arm the incoming names are the plan's component-function names, so the stored positional slot 'tool-2' read as 'dropped entirely' while the same component sat in the set as 'tool-loan-vs-savings' (resolved id and all), and the rescue arm appended the stored bytes with ComponentID '' (RFC_046 opt-in OFF). The lock guard then — working correctly — consumed the lock on the plan's entry and could not pair the appended one: the orphan. This is the THIRD of the save path's three 'already in the set' judgements; matchLockedRow was given an identity arm (182/189/204) and MergeLockedPageSlots was born mirroring it (LOCK-008); this one never was, and bugs_closed/189's own 'STILL OPEN' note predicted the survivor on 08-03. The fix gives the third matcher the same arms, from data its preload already fetches, extracted so tests execute the production decision. The armed population is 1 row fleet-wide (the victim's own locked row, still armed); the next build-arm rebuild of that page reproduces the damage until this lands.

plan.summary: save_page_sections' Layer 2 interactive-preservation matcher judges 'is this stored tool already represented in the incoming set?' by exact slot-name string, so on the build arm (incoming names = plan function names) a positionally-named stored tool reads as dropped and its stored bytes are re-appended beside the row the lock guard just correctly preserved — bugs_open/385's byte-identical NULL-component orphan. This change extracts that decision into matchPreservedSectionIdx and gives it the same arms as its two siblings (matchLockedRow's identity arm; MergeLockedPageSlots' function arm), with per-row consumption, using fields the Layer 2 preload already SELECTs. The three outcome arms (keep / splice / re-append) are unchanged; only the pairing verdict changes. Tests execute the extracted production decision and were mutation-verified red against the pre-fix behaviour.

edits.rationale: Extract the Layer 2 pairing decision with matchLockedRow's arms in matchLockedRow's order: component identity first (enrichSectionsWithComponentIDs runs at :397, before Layer 2, so plan-named sections carry resolved ids), then slot exact (pre-385 behaviour, kept), then kebab-normalised slot (the 041 naming landmine, as both siblings), then stored componentFunction vs incoming name (MergeLockedPageSlots' arm 3 — decides the 385 shape when the incoming side failed to enrich). Non-empty guards exactly as the siblings have, so an empty id or name never pairs. A claimed map gives each stored row at most one incoming section — the consumption rule both siblings already have — so two stored instances of one component against a composition naming it once pair one-to-one and the second is re-appended (preserved) rather than silently judged present.

Rewire the Layer 2 loop to decide through the extracted matcher and record claims. The three outcome arms are byte-unchanged. Also corrects the two comments the fix falsifies-or-strengthens: the dedup block's 'Nothing below can re-introduce a duplicate under this key' (true only under name identity — 385 proved slot-name absence is not absence) and the Layer 2 header's definition of 'does not reproduce' (now judged by the matcher, with the 385 citation so the next reader inherits the reason).

Tests that execute the production decision (WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-19: a test that mirrors the construction proves nothing). Six unit tests on matchPreservedSectionIdx — the motivating 385 shape via the identity arm, the function arm under failed enrichment, slot-exact and kebab regressions, empty-identity refusal, one-row-one-claim — all verified RED under the slot-name-only mutation. A source-scan wiring pin (same pattern as TestSplice_UsesAdoptCarriedProvenance) because re-inlining a slot comparison would revert production while unit tests stay green. One whole-action sqlmock test driving the exact 08-23 shape end to end: one hero INSERT, lock consumed by the incoming tool via the identity arm, nothing appended. Its comment records, deliberately, that the action-level test is NOT the mutation detector: under mutation the insert loop swallows the unexpected orphan INSERT (Warn + continue) — a guard in series, measured while writing it — so the unit tests and the wiring scan carry the mutation load.
edits.sketch: TestMatchPreservedSectionIdx_IdentityArmPairsPlanNamedSectionWithPositionalSlot: stored {slot:'tool-2', componentID:448422ce…, componentFunction:'tool-loan-vs-savings'} vs incoming [{hero,id…}, {name:'tool-loan-vs-savings', id:448422ce…}, {ported-prose}] => want 1; returns -1 on pre-fix code, which is exactly the 'dropped entirely' verdict that appended the orphan.

plan.risks: 1) A stored row that USED to be judged 'dropped' (and re-appended) can now match by identity/function and take the keep-or-splice arms instead — that is the fix, but a reviewer should confirm the splice arm's semantics are acceptable for an identity-matched non-interactive incoming section (it splices the stored bytes over it, exactly as it already does for a slot-name match; bugs_open/357's provenance hygiene, adoptCarriedProvenance, applies unchanged and its four existing tests stay green). 2) The claimed map is new consumption bookkeeping: two preserved rows can no longer both match one incoming section. Pre-fix, two stored rows sharing one slot name could both match index i — with slot names unique per page that was unreachable in practice; the new rule is the siblings' one-to-one pairing. 3) The empty-slot guard is a strict tightening: pre-fix, a stored row with slot_name '' could match an incoming section with ComponentName '' and take the splice arm; now empty never pairs, so such a row is re-appended (preserved) instead — the conservative direction for a preservation mechanism. 4) Behaviour on the rerender arm is unchanged (incoming names are slot names; the slot-exact arm sits where it always was, and the 08-25 24-page rerender wave is the field baseline). 5) The whole-action test suite for this file (stored-slot identity, 189 regression, dedup, floors, decision gate, claims, provenance) passes unchanged; the one failing test in the package, findingcodes_scan_test on WORK_ITEM_STATUS_OVERRIDE_REFUSED, predates this change (commit 2b46afbe6, the 396 lane) and is unrelated.
